conviction_note: The evidence offsets. HAL's Q3 (Middle East/Asia +8% sequentially on Saudi and Kuwait, and Q4 Middle East growth guided) supports SLB's Q3 base case and its preliminary Q4 Middle East recovery. Against that, Weatherford's MENA/Asia was flat and its CEO said recent Middle East events had dampened hopes of a quick recovery, after the September Hormuz tanker attacks and Houthi strikes on Saudi energy sites. The Q4 bar is also disputed: Q4 consensus of $10.06bn/$0.80 matches management's July 'above $10bn, ~24% margin' view, while Ortex reports 2026 EBITDA marked down to $8.0bn, which implies the street has already cut Q4. So p_up is 50. abs_move is 4.5, a little above the 4.18 event-implied move, because this print turns on a Q4 Middle East guide and probably a first 2027 view. The findings sum to +0.4 and the scaled number is 0.0. The gap is small and comes from the balance, not from a conflict.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus is $9.27bn and adjusted EPS $0.62 (Investing.com 2026-10-22 https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/slb-faces-earnings-test-as-international-deals-meet-profit-pressure-93CH-4966683 ; Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SLB/earnings-forecasts, the same figures, seen via search snippet only because the page returned 403). Company guide from the July 24 call: Q3 revenue +3-4% sequentially on Q2's $8.97bn, i.e. $9.24-9.33bn, with adjusted EBITDA margin up ~75bp from 21.2%. The downside case is flat Middle East revenue, which would mean about -$150m revenue and -$75m EBITDA (https://finance.biggo.com/quote/SLB/earnings-call/US_SLB_2026-07-24 ; https://longbridge.com/news/293770123). Consensus therefore sits mid-guide. Preliminary Q4 view from the same call: revenue above $10bn, ~24% EBITDA margin, Middle East revenue $2.1-2.2bn (~95% of Q4 2025). Q4 consensus is $10.06bn / $0.80 (Benzinga). The Q4 bar is disputed: Ortex (2026-10-20, https://ortex.news/articles/192472/slb-heads-into-q3-print-with-analysts-trimming-targets) reports 2026 EBITDA marked down to $8.0bn from $8.4bn, which implies a Q4 well below 24% margin, so findings that depend on Q4 are capped small. Zacks ESP is -1.45% and EPS estimates are -0.85% over 60 days.
positioning_check: Short interest about 3.9% of free float, down ~0.8% over the week. Borrow cost is 0.52%, with ample availability. Put/call ratio 0.67 against a 20-day average of 0.64 (Ortex, 2026-10-20, https://ortex.news/articles/192472/slb-heads-into-q3-print-with-analysts-trimming-targets). Curved Trading's July 15 2026 settlement shows ~63.2m shares short and 5.7 days to cover (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/slb/short-interest/). This is not a crowded short. Baseline: 25-delta skew is +2.11 vol points (downside modestly paid), the put/call open-interest ratio 1.31, and the event-implied move 4.18%. The stock is -3.9% over 20 days, +2.2% over 5 days and -17.8% from its 52-week high. Spot was 49.415 at 17:08 UTC on 10-22, after quotes of $51.10 earlier, so it was down roughly 3-4% on the day before the print. I could not source the cause of that day's drop.

findings.finding: Halliburton (released 2026-10-20) reported Q3 2026 Middle East/Asia revenue of $1.4bn, +8% sequentially, 'driven by higher activity across multiple product service lines in Saudi Arabia and Kuwait'. It guided Q4 Middle East revenue up both sequentially and year over year, and gave an early 2027 view of mid-single-digit revenue growth. SLB's Q3 base case of +3-4% sequential revenue (consensus $9.27bn, mid-guide) assumes a gradual Middle East recovery, and its Q4 view needs Middle East revenue of $2.1-2.2bn against Q2's $1.66bn. A direct peer's Saudi/Kuwait growth, landing after SLB last spoke, makes the base case more likely than the flat-Middle-East downside (-$150m revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-24): revenue beat consensus by ~3.5% with a Middle East recovery path laid out, and the stock rose +11.0% (baseline). The three prior prints moved +2.6%, -0.3% and -0.9%. Middle East-driven quarters have been the large movers.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. HAL rose ~3% in the week of its print (Ortex 10-20), yet SLB is still -3.9% over 20 days, sell-side targets were trimmed into the print, and EPS estimates drifted down 0.85% in 60 days. If the market had fully carried HAL's Saudi/Kuwait read into SLB, the estimates would have drifted up, not down. Consensus revenue still sits at mid-guide rather than the top.
findings.independence: SLB won four multi-year Aramco integrated well construction contracts (450+ wells) on 2026-09-24 (https://www.slb.com/newsroom/press-release/2026/pr-2026-0924-slb-aramco), a separate document pointing at a Saudi ramp. Weatherford's MENA/Asia figure points the other way (separate finding).

findings.finding: Weatherford (Q3 2026, released 2026-10-20) reported MENA/Asia revenue of $447m, flat sequentially and -16% year over year. Its CEO wrote that 'recent events in the Middle East have dampened expectations of a quick recovery'. This bears on SLB's preliminary Q4 view from July (revenue above $10bn, ~24% EBITDA margin, Middle East $2.1-2.2bn = ~95% of Q4 2025, from $1.66bn in Q2), which Q4 consensus of $10.06bn / $0.80 still mirrors. The risk is that SLB trims its Q4 Middle East assumption on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Q2 print SLB set the Q4 Middle East recovery path and rose +11%. That guide is what the stock has been holding on to. No cited instance of SLB cutting a Middle East guide is in the baseline window. In the 2025 prints (former name, outside the baseline) management cut regional expectations several times, but I have no sourced reaction for them.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Citi, Piper and Barclays trimmed targets in mid-October (Ortex 10-20) and the stock is 17.8% off its high with downside skew at +2.1. Q4 consensus revenue ($10.06bn) and EPS ($0.80, +29% sequentially) still sit on management's July view, though. If the street had priced a delayed Middle East recovery, Q4 consensus would sit below $10bn. The Q4 bar is disputed (Ortex reports 2026 EBITDA cut to $8.0bn), so this is capped small.
findings.independence: The September escalation (separate finding) is the event Weatherford refers to. HAL's Q4 Middle East guide points the opposite way and is a different document. The cuts in Ortex's analyst-target summary are consistent with this finding.

findings.finding: The Gulf re-escalated inside SLB's Q3. On 2026-09-01 two supertankers carrying Saudi oil were struck in the Strait of Hormuz. On ~2026-09-08 Houthi missile and drone strikes hit Saudi energy facilities and temporarily forced some operations to stop. SLB's own July downside scenario was exactly 'renewed disruption leaves Middle East revenue flat': about -$150m revenue (-1.6% vs the $9.27bn consensus) and -$75m EBITDA, roughly -$0.04 EPS against the $0.62 bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: Middle East revenue fell 13% sequentially, yet total revenue beat and the stock rose 11%, because the market looked through a disruption it had expected. The reported Middle East line has not been sold on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The attacks were headline news and EPS estimates drifted only -0.85%. What is not visible is how much of SLB's base case survived September. HAL's Saudi/Kuwait +8% says activity held at a peer, which is why this is sized small and net of that document.
findings.independence: Houthi strikes on Saudi energy facilities, reported 2026-09-08 (https://www.foxnews.com/politics/iran-backed-attacks-threaten-second-major-oil-chokepoint-new-risk-emerges-us-consumers). This shares its event set with the Weatherford finding but lands on the reported quarter rather than the Q4 guide. HAL's document partly contradicts it.

findings.finding: Contract awards since the July print support the backlog and 2027 commentary on the call: four multi-year Aramco integrated well construction contracts covering 450+ wells over an initial three years (2026-09-24), a major OQEP integrated facility expansion in Oman (2026-09-22), and a 15-year TotalEnergies DrillPlan digital agreement (2026-10-08). The Aramco award points to a Saudi drilling ramp into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no cited instance of an award announcement moving the stock on a print. The +11% in July came with a forward Middle East recovery narrative of the kind these awards support.
findings.why_not_priced: The awards are public, but their values were not disclosed, so no estimate can include them. The stock fell over the 20 days after them (-3.9%) instead of rising. Once management quantifies backlog or Saudi activity on the call, the market can price them.
findings.independence: OQEP Oman award (https://secure.businesswire.com/news/home/20260922635677/en/SLB-Awarded-Major-Contract-by-OQEP-for-Integrated-Facility-Expansion-in-Oman) and TotalEnergies DrillPlan (https://www.slb.com/newsroom/press-release/2026/pr-2026-1008-total-energies-drillplan). These are separate company documents with the same issuer. HAL's Saudi/Kuwait growth is an independent pointer.

findings.finding: North America softened in Q3. HAL's North America revenue was $2.2bn, -5% sequentially, and its Completion & Production segment -4%. Ortex's preview carries SLB North America as flat sequentially. SLB's North America is ~19% of revenue and production-weighted (ChampionX chemicals, artificial lift), so it is less exposed to frac activity than HAL's. Net of that mix, this is a small drag on a line that consensus already treats as flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: North America has not been the line SLB traded on in the four baseline prints. International and Middle East commentary dominated.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. HAL's print is public and the preview already assumes flat. It is kept small because the production-weighted mix is a reason it could still land worse or better.
findings.independence: This shares a document with the HAL Middle East finding (different line). Weatherford's North America was +15% sequentially (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001603923/000160392326000118/a2026-q3ex991earningsrelea.htm), which points the other way.

findings.finding: The bar has been lowered into the print. Citi cut its target to $62, Piper Sandler to $63 and Barclays to $66 in mid-October, all keeping Buy ratings. EPS estimates are -0.85% over 60 days and -0.73% over the last week, and Zacks ESP is -1.45%. The stock is -17.8% off its 52-week high and fell ~3-4% on 10-22, from $51.10 quoted to $49.4. SLB has beaten EPS four quarters running (average surprise 4.9%; Q2 $0.55 vs $0.51-0.52).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a lowered bar in Q2 (Middle East disruptions cut guidance by $0.06-0.08), a beat produced +11%. The other three beats moved within ±2.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Target cuts and estimate drift are public. The point is that they lower the hurdle, which a stock trading at the bottom of its recent range with downside skew paid has not yet re-rated against. If the market expected a beat, the skew would not be +2.1 and the stock would not have slid into the print.
findings.independence: Investing.com preview 2026-10-22 (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/slb-faces-earnings-test-as-international-deals-meet-profit-pressure-93CH-4966683) carries the same target cuts and the revisions.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-31 SLB agreed to buy Kelvion (thermal management for data centers) for ~$3.4bn cash plus $0.7bn of debt, closing in H1 2027. In the same release it said it would return more than $4bn to shareholders in 2026 and expected 2027 returns 'at least in line with 2026 levels', with formal targets to come later. The financing question: the cash buys a data center ramp corroborated by SLB's own Data Center Solutions (+33% sequentially in Q2, '>$1bn run rate by year-end'), and leverage stays inside the 1.5x target. If formal 2027 return targets come with this print, that is a modest positive.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no sourced instance of a capital-return announcement moving the stock on a print in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The deal and the 'at least in line' statement are public. What is not known is whether formal 2027 numbers come now or in January. Had a 2027 buyback step-up been expected, it would show in previews, and none mention it.
findings.independence: World Oil 2026-08-31 (https://www.worldoil.com/news/2026/8/31/slb-expands-data-center-business-with-4-1-billion-kelvion-acquisition/) reprints the same release, so it is not independent.

findings.finding: Data Center Solutions grew +33% sequentially in Q2. Management said in the July release that it 'remains on track to exceed $1 billion annualized revenue run rate by the end of this year'. Q3 should show progress inside that guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line was part of the July beat narrative (+11%). It is too small (~2-3% of revenue) to be the line the stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: It lands inside what the company already guided, so it is sized near zero.
findings.independence: Same company document as the Q2 release. The Kelvion release restates the data center targets.

outside_window.finding: Kelvion acquisition closing (H1 2027, pending regulatory approvals): integration and financing effects arrive after the exit window.
Baker Hughes Q3 2026 results (OFSE international read-through) are released 2026-10-27 at 17:00 ET, after SLB's exit window.

baseline_tension: The skew (+2.1, downside paid) and the 17.8% drawdown agree with the Weatherford and September-escalation negatives. HAL's Saudi/Kuwait growth, the Aramco awards and the lowered bar cut against them, and the net is roughly flat. Nothing here is strong enough to argue the option market is wrong in either direction.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar disputed): the Q4 bar is disputed (Q4 consensus $10.06bn/$0.80 vs Ortex's 2026 EBITDA cut to $8.0bn), so the Q4-dependent Weatherford guidance finding was capped from -1.2 to -0.9 and the HAL finding trimmed from +1.0 to +0.9; p_up moved from 49 to 50
Lesson 3 / 5 (own caveat; documents beat inference): the September-escalation finding is partly contradicted by HAL's document showing Saudi/Kuwait activity up in Q3, so it went from -0.6 to -0.4
Lesson 9 (segment net of the rest): HAL's North America read applies to only ~19% of SLB's revenue, which is production-weighted, so it went from -0.3 to -0.2
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the contract awards are public with undisclosed values, so they went from +0.5 to +0.4, and the lowered-bar positioning finding from +0.4 to +0.3
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the Kelvion cash buys a data center ramp corroborated by DCS growth, so it was left at +0.2 and signed positive
Lesson 7: short interest checked (3.9% of float, not crowded) and no negative was shrunk for squeeze risk
